title: operations.orders.order.invoice_requested
description: Operations asks finance to raise the invoice for one accepted order, naming a price snapshot finance must agree with before it acts (Fulfilment ADR-0024 §1/§4). `customer_id` is a `finance.customers.id`, already resolved from whatever CRM contact placed the order — not a CRM reference finance would have to resolve itself. `tax_rate_pct` is the document-level GST rate every line inherits unless it states its own; finance's `domain.split_gst` needs a rate to recompute tax from, so this field exists even though it was not in this event's first draft. Money is integer minor units of `currency`. `expected_subtotal_minor` is the sum of every line's `line_amount_minor`; `expected_tax_minor`/`expected_total_minor` are what operations computed the GST and grand total to be. Finance recomputes all three from `lines`, `place_of_supply` and `supply_type`, and refuses — `finance.orders.invoice.request_rejected` — on anything but exact agreement.
$comment: Produced by operations' `app.consumers.order_invoice_due` (INVENTORY-01), which resolves `customer_id` through finance's `customers:resolve-for-crm-contact`. Operations omits `place_of_supply` and `supply_type`; finance then derives both from the billed party, as for an invoice raised by hand.

customer_id.description: A `finance.customers.id` for this organization — already resolved, not a CRM contact id.

line_amount_minor.description: The line's taxable value — the price snapshot GST is computed on. Taken as given, not re-derived from quantity x unit_price_minor.

tax_rate_pct.description: Overrides the request's own tax_rate_pct for this one line. Omitted or null inherits it.
The document-level GST rate every line inherits unless it states its own.

place_of_supply.description: A GST state code. Omitted or null: finance uses the buyer's GSTIN state, then the buyer's state, then the seller's own state.

supply_type.description: Omitted: finance uses b2b when the billed party has a GSTIN on file, otherwise b2c.
